data.one_liner: Render HTML content as native Flutter widgets with support for common tags, CSS, and media.
data.what_it_does: Parses HTML strings into a tree of Flutter widgets. It supports 70+ HTML tags, inline CSS styling, hyperlinks, images, audio, video, and iframes.
use_when: You need to display blog posts, article text, or rich HTML content directly inside a Flutter app.
You want to render custom HTML fragments that include formatting, lists, tables, and media elements.
avoid_when: You are building a full-featured web browser application where complex JavaScript and DOM interaction are required.
You want to keep app size minimal and do not need full HTML/CSS rendering capabilities.
strengths: Extensive support for common HTML tags, CSS styles, and counter-styles.
Modular architecture allowing core usage or optional extensions for caching images, audio, video, and webviews.
Provides callbacks for handling user interactions like link and image taps.
weaknesses: Some native media dependencies (like audio) require platform-specific permissions or podfile configurations.
Complex CSS and extensive HTML parsing can introduce performance overhead on very large documents.
data.setup_notes: iOS microphone permissions may be required if audio tag support via just_audio is included.

alternatives.name: flutter_widget_from_html_core
alternatives.why_pick_it: Choose this core package instead if you want a lighter build and want to manually select a subset of feature mixins.
